The court will require a greater foundation to establish the reliability of the records, because the defendant's bare testimony that they were kept on a regular business basis does not satisfy the business-records exception's requirements (such as showing the records were made contemporaneously by someone with knowledge, in the regular course of business) or authenticate the computer records. The hearsay objection is not dismissed merely because the defendant is available, since availability alone does not excuse the foundational showing.
CONFIDENCE: 90
